prompt.context:
The client is a leading TV/film studio that has several lines of business. They are particularly concerned about one part of their business which provides postproduction services internally as well as for external customers. This division has experienced stagnating profits in recent times. They have hired you to explore ways to address this problem and increase the profitability of this business.

The postproduction services division is comprised of four distinct products:
- Restoration of old films for preservation
- Production of master prints for theaters and exhibition
- Production of master copies for the home entertainment market
- Production of daily material for review during ongoing film production

It is common in the movie industry to outsource these functions. However, based on the studio's market research, their internal rates for these services are comparable to market rates. The CFO wants to know what strategic options he has to increase profitability.
prompt.question:
1. Which possible recommendations will you consider for each business unit?
2. Which criteria would you use for the recommendations?
3. What metrics would you use to determine the relative profitability of the four services?

clarifying_info.q: Are there any data on revenues and costs for each service line?
clarifying_info.a: Yes — see Exhibit A, which shows revenues and COGS for each of the four services.

clarifying_info.q: Are there data on the volume or number of jobs per service?
clarifying_info.a: Yes — see Exhibit B, which shows the number of jobs per service in the most recent quarter.

clarifying_info.q: What do customers care about most for each service?
clarifying_info.a: Restoration customers care primarily about quality. Master Theatre, Master Home, and New Productions customers care about both quality and price. Dailies customers care primarily about speed of service.

clarifying_info.q: What is the trend in the market for these services?
clarifying_info.a: Restoration and Dailies markets are stable. The Master Theatre and Master Home markets have been decreasing in recent times.
SG&A costs have been stable and are shared among the service lines. A recent benchmark study shows these costs are consistent with industry norms.

clarifying_info.q: Should we consider outsourcing any of these services?
clarifying_info.a: Since internal rates are comparable to market rates, there are no monetary benefits from outsourcing, so it should not be a primary concern.

exhibits.title: Revenues and COGS for Print Production Services
exhibits.shows: A bar chart displaying revenues and COGS (in millions) for each of the four postproduction service lines: Dailies, Master Home, Master Theatre, and Restoration.

exhibits.title: Volume — Number of Jobs (Most Recent Quarter)
exhibits.shows: A table showing the number of jobs completed in the most recent quarter for each service line.

framework: Assess profitability of each service line: calculate gross margin = (Revenue - COGS) / Revenue using Exhibit A data
Evaluate strategic dimensions for each service: market trend (growing/stable/declining), nature of business (core vs. non-core), contribution to total revenue
Generate strategic options per service line: Expand, Boost revenues (marketing), Lower costs (operations), Keep as-is, Explore for improvement, Close, Sell, or Spin-off
Apply decision criteria consistently across all four service lines: gross profit margin, market trend, revenue contribution, core/non-core classification, ease of implementation, competitive risk
Conduct risk analysis: assess competitive responses to any strategic action (e.g., competitors bundling services if one line is dropped)
Address SG&A allocation and implementation/next steps

questions.prompt: Calculate the gross profit margin for each of the four service lines using Exhibit A.
questions.guidance: Candidate must use gross margin = (Revenue - COGS) / Revenue. Comparing only total revenues or total COGS is insufficient and should be flagged. Exhibit B (volume/jobs data) is intentionally provided as a potential distraction — using it to compute per-job economics is a valid but unnecessary complication; the interviewer should note this as constructive feedback.

math.setup: Gross Margin = (Revenue - COGS) / Revenue for each service line (figures in millions)
math.answer: Restoration: 55% | Master Theatre: 23% | Master Home: 10% | Dailies: 40%

questions.prompt: Based on the profitability data and market trends, what strategic recommendation do you make for each service line?
questions.guidance: Candidate should combine financial metrics (gross margin, revenue contribution) with strategic context (market trend, customer priorities, core vs. non-core, competitive risk). Restoration (55% margin, stable market, quality-focused) → Keep and Expand. Dailies (40% margin, stable market, speed-focused) → Keep and Expand. Master Theatre (23% margin, declining market) → Keep but monitor. Master Home (10% margin, declining market, largest revenue but thinnest margin) → Explore options: cost reduction, pricing review, or strategic exit. A strong candidate will also note the risk of exiting any service — competitors may bundle services and attract clients away.

questions.prompt: What criteria should be used to evaluate recommendations across the four service lines?
questions.guidance: Strong answer covers multiple dimensions: (1) gross profit margin, (2) contribution to total revenues, (3) nature of service — core vs. non-core to the studio's strategy, (4) market trend (growing/stable/declining), (5) ease of implementation of proposed solution, (6) risk — including competitive responses such as rivals bundling services to capture clients if the studio exits a segment.

questions.prompt: What metrics determine relative profitability of the four services?
questions.guidance: Primary metric: gross profit margin = (Revenue - COGS) / Revenue. Secondary metrics: absolute profit dollars per service, revenue contribution as a percentage of total division revenue, and optionally per-job profitability (though this adds unnecessary complexity given the available data). SG&A is shared and benchmarked as industry-standard, so it does not differentiate between lines at this stage.

brainstorming.prompt: What risks or competitive responses should the studio consider when deciding to exit or restructure a service line?

categories.name: Competitive bundling risk
ideas: Competitors may bundle all four postproduction services and offer package discounts
Clients who currently split work across vendors may consolidate to a single vendor offering bundles
Exiting even a low-margin service could trigger client defection across higher-margin lines

categories.name: Revenue interdependency
ideas: Dailies (daily review) and Master prints may be purchased together by the same production
Losing one service contract may cause the client to move all postproduction work to a competitor
Cross-selling opportunities across service lines would be lost

categories.name: Strategic and operational risks
ideas: Exiting a service line may be difficult to reverse if market conditions improve later
Workforce and specialized equipment may need to be written off
SG&A currently shared across lines — exiting one line increases cost burden on remaining lines

categories.name: Market response and positioning
ideas: Price reductions to boost volume in declining segments could trigger a price war
Investing in technology upgrades for Master Home may improve margins but requires upfront capital
Differentiating on quality for Restoration and speed for Dailies can defend margins without price competition

recommendation: Expand Restoration (55% margin, stable market, quality-driven — invest in capacity and marketing to external clients)
Expand Dailies (40% margin, stable market, speed-driven — invest in turnaround time and client relationships)
Keep Master Theatre under active monitoring (23% margin, declining market — maintain but do not invest heavily; pursue cost efficiencies)

Conduct deep-dive on Master Home (10% margin, declining market, largest revenue base — explore cost reduction, selective repricing, or strategic exit while assessing bundling risk before any exit decision)
risks: Exiting Master Home could trigger competitive bundling by rivals, risking client relationships across all four service lines
Declining market trend for Master services may accelerate if streaming/digital distribution erodes physical print demand
SG&A reallocation if any service is discontinued could increase cost burden on remaining lines
next_steps: Conduct detailed cost analysis to identify COGS reduction opportunities in Master Home
Evaluate whether external customer base for Restoration and Dailies can be expanded to boost revenue
Assess competitive landscape and likelihood of bundling strategies from rivals before any exit
Address SG&A allocation methodology to ensure accurate profitability measurement per service line
Define implementation timeline and KPIs for each recommendation
